summary.headline: Nothing is INVALID/pull. M-01 survives both candidate rejection vectors (reckless-admin: NO via surprise-test; KI#8: distinguishable but is the sharpest residual risk and must be disclosed). 3 QA-tier items (L-05, QA-02, C-01) flagged WEAK for honest down-weighting, none pulled.

findings.title: Fail-open unconfigured-token default -> zero-payment 100% yield drain (symmetric reward-token brick)
findings.caveat: KI#8-overlap is the primary residual rejection risk and MUST be disclosed prominently; submission already does so.

checks.note: USDC/USDT are standard ERC-20s; bug is SYA's own fail-open config handling, not weird-token behavior. USDT is in any case the carve-out exception. Not invalid on this axis.
Drain does not depend on transfer fees. The separate 4naly3er M-1 FoT flag is correctly suppressed (no FoT token in scope) and is NOT this finding.
Claimer calls a permissionless function correctly; no user input error, no phishing. The owner config omission is the precondition, not a user mistake.

checks.ruling: NOT a reckless-admin finding. See adminSurpriseTest below — this is a NON-OBVIOUS owner footgun (Law 3 in-scope), not owner malice and not an obvious-harm misconfig.

checks.note: Root cause is entirely in-scope: _normalizeAmount/_denormalizeAmount fail-open fallbacks (L586-640) + missing config link in addYieldStrategy (L227) / setRewardToken (L360), all in src/StableYieldAccumulator.sol (the sole in-scope contract). skimSurplus delivers real value but the mispricing is SYA-side.
Passing Foundry PoC (2/2) on the real claim() path + halmos symbolic proof on real bytecode (SYMBOLIC-001/002). Not speculative; demonstrated root cause.

checks.ruling: DISTINGUISHABLE from KI#8 (and not KI#2/#4/#5) — see knownIssueAdjudication. This is the SHARPEST rejection vector; keep VALID but disclose.

adminSurpriseTest.question: Would a competent, non-malicious owner be SURPRISED that forgetting one setTokenConfig hands 100% of a 6-dec strategy's yield to any NFT holder for zero payment?
adminSurpriseTest.verdict: SURPRISE => FOOTGUN => VALID (in-scope operational hazard, not reckless-admin)
nonObviousSignals: No enforcement: addYieldStrategy(strategy, token) takes no decimals arg and never requires a TokenConfig; setRewardToken never requires one. Nothing links registration/funding to config.
No revert: the misconfiguration succeeds silently — the owner gets no error at config time.
Active masking: calculateClaimAmount() previews 0, so a careful owner who checks the preview sees what looks like 'no yield yet', NOT 'misconfigured/draining'. There is no signal anywhere.
Fail-OPEN to a plausible-looking value: (0,0) resolves to 18-dec 1:1, which is CORRECT for many tokens but catastrophically wrong for the 6-dec stables this 'stable yield accumulator' is built for.
Two-step config: decimals live in a separate, easy-to-forget call from registration.
adminSurpriseTest.whyNotObvious: The obviousness test is NOT 'should the owner have configured the token' (trivially yes) but 'would the owner be surprised by the CONSEQUENCE'. A competent owner forgetting one setter among many would expect at worst a revert or zero yield — NOT a silent, permissionless, repeatable 100% theft that the on-chain preview reports as 0. The consequence is non-obvious; the owner is non-malicious. Textbook Law-3 footgun, explicitly distinct from the suppressed malicious-owner C-01 framing.
adminSurpriseTest.whyNotMalicious: Requires zero malice — only a forgotten setter. Attacker is an ordinary NFT holder, not the owner. This is NOT a 'malicious owner could...' vector (those are correctly suppressed under C-01/KI#5).

KI#8.text: Token config with zero decimals and zero exchange rate defaults to 18 decimals and 1:1 rate
KI#8.rebuttal: KI#8 documents the default-RESOLUTION RULE (what the (0,0) struct resolves to) as a config convenience — you need not explicitly configure an 18-dec/1:1 token. It does NOT document the CONSEQUENCE: that applying this default to a registered SUB-18-decimal strategy token silently breaks value conservation and hands 100% of that strategy's yield to any claimer for zero payment (and the symmetric reward-token brick). A known issue excludes a finding only when the sponsor acknowledged the RISK, not merely the MECHANISM; here the sponsor stated the mechanism as benign default sugar.
KI#8.honestResidual: This is the strongest plausible rejection vector — a strict C4 judge could rule that documenting the exact (0,0)->18-dec mechanism is enough to make the drain 'known/OOS'. The distinction (documented value vs. documented consequence) is legitimate but not bulletproof. PER LAW 1 (recall beats tidiness) we KEEP M-01, and the submission's 'Relationship to known issues' section already discloses this debate prominently — correct handling. Do NOT pull; DO surface the KI#8 caveat in the final summary so it is adjudicated in the open, not buried.

KI#2.note: Blesses the normalization MATH for CONFIGURED tokens only; says nothing about the unconfigured/in-use case. Accurate per submission.

KI#4_KI#5.note: Cover the depeg/discount owner-drain framing (the separate, suppressed C-01 centralization item, a malicious-owner root cause). M-01 needs no malice and is a different root cause. Accurate per submission.

findings.notes: Severity (Medium top-of-band vs Plausible-High dissent) is the severity-auditor's call, not a validity question; recorded and out of scope for this gate. Validity verdict: KEEP.

findings.title: setNudgeSplit(>0) without nudge!=0 guard bricks every yielding claim (NudgeNotConfigured)

checks.ruling: NON-OBVIOUS config-ordering footgun, not an obvious admin error and not malice.

checks.note: Root cause is the write-side enforcement gap in setNudgeSplit (L396-402) + setNudgeAddress (L385-389), in-scope.

Root cause read directly from source: setter checks only _split>100, while the coupling invariant is enforced only on the read side at claim() L506. No PoC required for a recoverable Low availability footgun.

adminSurpriseTest.question: Would a competent owner be surprised that enabling the split before wiring the recipient (or clearing the recipient while a split is active) bricks every yielding claim?
adminSurpriseTest.reasoning: The setter accepts the value with no error; the NATURAL config order (enable feature, then point it at a recipient) lands in the broken state; the write side does not enforce the invariant the read side (L506) relies on — an asymmetry a careful owner would not anticipate. Brick is fail-SAFE (atomic revert, no NFT consumed, no funds move) and immediately owner-recoverable by a single setter. Non-obvious enough + low-impact + recoverable => correctly Low, not an invalid obvious-misconfig.

findings.notes: Borderline on the obviousness axis, but the write-side/read-side asymmetry is genuine technical substance and the outcome is fail-safe/recoverable. KEEP at Low in the QA bundle.

findings.title: claim/preview gas scales with (strategies x authorized-clients); consolidation can stall above the discount-vs-gas threshold

checks.note: econ-scanner CORRECTED the static/pattern 'anyone depositing grows the set' premise: addYieldStrategy is onlyOwner and IYieldStrategy.setClient is strategy-owner-gated, so NO external party can force the stall. Not a permissionless DoS.

checks.ruling: IN-SCOPE LOCUS IS ENOUGH (keep), but caveat: the gas-growth TRIGGER (client cardinality) comes from strategy.getAuthorizedClients() — an external, owner-gated dimension touching KI#7. The ROOT CAUSE of the scaling is SYA's own nested loop (claim L464 / _getYieldForStrategy L556), which is in scope, so KI#7 does not fully cover it. Severity is correctly capped at Low precisely because the growth dimension is OOS/privileged, not permissionless.

checks.note: Static + interface reasoning; confidence: medium. Self-correcting (owner raises discount / prunes strategies; exemptStrategies mitigates single-strategy pathologies).

findings.weakRationale: Operational gas-scaling with NO permissionless trigger, self-correcting, owner/strategy-owner-bounded, and partly leaning on OOS client growth (KI#7). Legitimately in scope via SYA's own loop, but it is near the QA/informational floor. Keep at Low in the QA bundle; do NOT escalate. Honest down-weight, not a pull.

findings.title: Preview-vs-actual divergence with no payment ceiling; getTotalYield ignores per-token pause (no profitable sandwich)

checks.note: econ-scanner concluded NO profitable sandwich (an attacker inflating actualPayment by donating surplus also gifts the victim discount*donation). Pattern-matcher's potential-high/medium framings correctly down-weighted. Not overstated.

Facet (a) no-max-ceiling is a claimer-side self-DoS driven by a DOCUMENTED design divergence (story-025) + a missing symmetric guard — a real ergonomic gap, not merely a user typo. Facet (b) getTotalYield omitting the paused skip is a clean in-scope view-consistency bug.

The strategy-side MAGNITUDE of the divergence roots in the OOS adapter (KI#7) and is explicitly scoped OUT; only the SYA-side slice (no ceiling at L501 + getTotalYield paused omission at L738) is reported. Correct scoping.

findings.notes: No value loss, no third-party griefing; legitimate Low QA. KEEP.

findings.title: First-claimer captures the accumulated discount; minRewardTokenSupplied defaults to 0

checks.note: The discount-capture IS the designed decentralized-conversion incentive (designDecisions[0]); the finding explicitly states 'None required for security' and is kept as INFORMATIONAL only, NOT escalated as a vuln. Per C4 this is the right disposition (intended design is not a bug); per Law 1 it is kept visible rather than silently dropped.

Explicitly down-weighted from pattern's potential-medium; first claim empties the pot so no sandwich exists. PATTERN-007 'nudge winner-take-all' ruled a red herring (nudge is a proportional share to an owner-set recipient).

findings.weakRationale: Mostly by-design/informational. The only substantive residual is the min=0 default disabling the per-claim floor (cross-ref L-01) — minor and claimer-self-harming. Fine as a QA-informational note; near-zero HM substance. Keep; do not promote.

findings.title: nonReentrant is not the first modifier on claim()
findings.severityVerdict: correctly QA/Informational; weakest item, most droppable

checks.ruling: Acknowledged contextual false-positive from a SINGLE static source (aderyn): whenNotPaused is a pure storage read with no external call/state change, so the ordering opens NO reentrancy window. No HM exploit path. CLAUDE.md treats automated-tool findings without a demonstrated HM path as OOS for promotion — correctly NOT promoted; retained only as a one-line defensive QA note (Law 1 recall).

findings.weakRationale: Pure defensive style note, zero impact, contextual FP. Acceptable as a one-liner in the QA bundle but adds little; this is the single most droppable item if trimming the QA report. Not invalid (claims no vuln); just low-value. Keep-or-drop is editorial.

findings.title: Owner configuration authority — unbounded exchange rate and up-to-100% discount (centralization-by-design)

checks.ruling: The CORE 'a malicious owner could set claimer payment to zero' capability is exactly the malicious-owner vector Law-3/C4 say must NOT be reported as a live vuln. The finding handles this correctly: the High framing is explicitly SUPPRESSED (dedup SUPPRESS-001), it is presented ONLY as a documented centralization residual (ledger C-01), and it is covered by KI#4 (1:1/depeg owner lever) and KI#5 (owner trust assumptions). C4 permits a centralization section in the QA bundle, so the disposition is conventional.

checks.note: Largely covered by KI#4 + KI#5; presented for completeness, not as a new finding.

findings.weakRationale: Borderline under strict Law-3 (a pure malicious-owner finding is noise) AND already in known issues. NOT pulled because (a) C4 conventionally allows a centralization disclosure in QA, and (b) its real added value is the ops guidance (multisig / timelock / Ownable2Step) and the cross-links to the genuine in-scope footguns M-01 and L-04. REQUIREMENT: keep all malicious-owner language framed as documented/accepted/suppressed (it currently is) — never as a live exploit. Do not re-escalate to High.
findings.guardrail: If the final report needs trimming, C-01 can be compressed to the ops-guidance + footgun cross-links; the malicious-owner capability paragraph must stay labeled centralization-by-design.

findings.title: claim() NatSpec pay-then-skim + direct claimer->phlimbo drift vs skim-then-pay + claimer->this->{nudge,phlimbo-pull}

checks.note: Not a weird-token / FoT / approve-race / user-mistake / admin / OOS-root-cause item. A legitimate Law-2 faithfulness deviation, documentation-only (securityEscalation:false, alsoSecurityImpact:false). claim() is nonReentrant+whenNotPaused so skim-then-pay is atomic and value conservation holds; reentrancy facet refuted (RESOLVED-002).
Verbatim spec text vs verbatim code lines cited on both sides. Concrete, not speculative.

findings.notes: Correctly routed to the spec-conformance channel (separate from QA), shares ledger L-03 fingerprint as the faithfulness facet, not a duplicate ledger entry. KEEP.

flagsForFinalSummary: M-01: KEEP. Two candidate rejection vectors adjudicated — (1) reckless-admin: NO, fails the surprise test (non-obvious footgun, owner non-malicious, preview masks it with a 0, no enforcement/revert); (2) KI#8 known-issue overlap: this is the SHARPEST residual risk — distinguishable (KI#8 documents the default VALUE, not the drain CONSEQUENCE) but not bulletproof; submission already discloses it. Surface the KI#8 caveat openly in the summary.

L-05, QA-02, C-01: WEAK — keep but down-weight honestly. L-05 leans partly on OOS client growth (KI#7) though its loop root cause is in scope; QA-02 is an acknowledged tool FP one-liner (most droppable); C-01 is a known-issue/centralization-by-design disclosure whose malicious-owner core is correctly suppressed.
No finding is INVALID. Nothing to pull. No malicious-owner vector is presented as a live vuln (C-01's is suppressed/labeled). No weird-token/FoT/approve-race/user-mistake/phishing finding present.
